HEADER_ROW = 5


def rd(name):
    with open(os.path.join(CLEAN, name), encoding="utf-8") as f:
        return list(csv.DictReader(f))


def active_products():
    """[(product, category, units, n_units, athlete_data, status)], in use or planned."""
    statuses = collections.defaultdict(set)
    for r in rd("tech_inventory_long.csv"):
        statuses[r["canonical"]].add(r["status"])
    rows = []
    for m in rd("tech_master.csv"):
        p = m["canonical"]
        if m["category"] == "excluded" or p in GENERIC:
            continue
        s = statuses.get(p, set())
        if s and s <= {"stopped"}:
            continue
        status = "Planned" if s == {"planned"} else "In use"
        units = "; ".join(u.strip() for u in m["units"].split(";") if u.strip())
        rows.append((p, m["category"], units, int(m["unit_count"] or 0),
                     "Yes" if m["athlete_data_likely"] == "Y" else "", status))
    return sorted(rows, key=lambda r: r[0].lower())


def stopped_by():
    """product -> {"cat", "units"} for every product some unit stopped using."""
    by = collections.defaultdict(lambda: {"cat": "", "units": set()})
    for r in rd("stopped_using.csv"):
        e = by[r["canonical"]]
        e["cat"] = r["category"]
        e["units"].add(r["unit"])
    return by


def retired_products(active_names):
    """Products no unit uses any more. One unit stopping Hudl does not retire Hudl;
    those stay on the main sheet with a note (see stopped_notes)."""
    return sorted(((p, e["cat"], "; ".join(sorted(e["units"])), len(e["units"]), "", "Retired")
                   for p, e in stopped_by().items() if p not in active_names),
                  key=lambda r: r[0].lower())


def stopped_notes(active_names):
    """product -> note, for products still in use elsewhere but dropped by some unit."""
    return {p: "Stopped in the last 12 months by: " + "; ".join(sorted(e["units"]))
            for p, e in stopped_by().items() if p in active_names}


def banner(ws, title, deck):
    last = get_column_letter(len(COLUMNS))
    ws["A1"] = "INTERNAL ONLY  |  BUDGET PLANNING GROUP  |  DO NOT FORWARD"
    ws["A1"].font = Font(name=FONT, size=9, bold=True, color=GOLD)
    ws["A2"] = title
    ws["A2"].font = Font(name=FONT, size=16, bold=True, color=GREEN)
    ws["A3"] = deck
    ws["A3"].font = Font(name=FONT, size=10, italic=True, color=GREY)
    for r in (1, 2, 3):
        ws.merge_cells(f"A{r}:{last}{r}")


def product_sheet(ws, rows, title, deck, total=True, notes=None):
    notes = notes or {}
    banner(ws, title, deck)
    for c, (name, width, kind) in enumerate(COLUMNS, 1):
        cell = ws.cell(HEADER_ROW, c, name)
        cell.font = Font(name=FONT, bold=True, color="FFFFFF")
        cell.fill = PatternFill("solid", fgColor=GREEN if kind is None else GOLD)
        cell.alignment = Alignment(wrap_text=True, vertical="center")
        ws.column_dimensions[get_column_letter(c)].width = width
    ws.row_dimensions[HEADER_ROW].height = 30

    yesno = DataValidation(type="list", formula1='"Yes,No,Unknown"', allow_blank=True)
    basis = DataValidation(type="list", allow_blank=True,
                           formula1='"Per year,Per seat per year,Per month,One-time,Included in other contract,Free"')
    for dv in (yesno, basis):
        ws.add_data_validation(dv)

    cream = PatternFill("solid", fgColor=CREAM)
    first = HEADER_ROW + 1
    for i, row in enumerate(rows):
        r = first + i
        known = KNOWN.get(row[0], {})
        for c, (name, _w, kind) in enumerate(COLUMNS, 1):
            cell = ws.cell(r, c, row[c - 1] if kind is None else None)
            cell.font = Font(name=FONT, size=10)
            cell.border = Border(bottom=THIN)
            cell.alignment = Alignment(vertical="top", wrap_text=(name in ("Units using it", "Notes")))
            if kind:
                cell.fill = cream
            if kind == "money":
                cell.number_format = '"$"#,##0.00'
            elif kind == "date":
                cell.number_format = "yyyy-mm-dd"
            elif kind == "int":
                cell.number_format = "0"
            elif kind == "yesno":
                yesno.add(cell)
            elif kind == "basis":
                basis.add(cell)
        if "term_end" in known:
            ws.cell(r, col("Term end"), known["term_end"])
        note = "; ".join(n for n in (known.get("notes"), notes.get(row[0])) if n)
        if note:
            ws.cell(r, col("Notes"), note)

    last = first + len(rows) - 1
    if total and rows:
        t = last + 2
        ws.cell(t, col("Product"), "Total annual cost (filled rows)").font = Font(name=FONT, bold=True, color=GREEN)
        m = get_column_letter(col("Annual cost ($)"))
        cell = ws.cell(t, col("Annual cost ($)"), f"=SUM({m}{first}:{m}{last})")
        cell.font = Font(name=FONT, bold=True, color=GREEN)
        cell.number_format = '"$"#,##0.00'
        filled = ws.cell(t + 1, col("Product"),
                         f'=COUNT({m}{first}:{m}{last})&" of {len(rows)} products have a cost"')
        filled.font = Font(name=FONT, size=9, italic=True, color=GREY)
    ws.freeze_panes = ws.cell(first, 2)
    ws.auto_filter.ref = f"A{HEADER_ROW}:{get_column_letter(len(COLUMNS))}{last}"
    ws.sheet_view.zoomScale = 90


def col(name):
    return next(i for i, c in enumerate(COLUMNS, 1) if c[0] == name)


def guide(ws, n_active, n_retired):
    lines = [
        ("How to fill this in", True),
        ("", False),
        ("Green columns come from the inventory survey. Do not edit them; corrections go to Eric.", False),
        ("Gold columns are for cost and contract details. Fill in as many as you can; blanks are fine.", False),
        ("Annual cost: what the department pays per year. For per-seat or monthly pricing, enter the yearly total and pick the cost basis.", False),
        ("Paid by: the unit or budget line that pays, as the Business Office records it.", False),
        ("Term end: the date the current contract or subscription ends. Notice to cancel: days of notice the vendor needs before that date.", False),
        ("Auto-renews: Yes, No, or Unknown. Unknown is better than a guess.", False),
        ("Notes: anything that matters for FY28 planning (price increase, overlap with another product, plan to drop).", False),
        ("", False),
        (f"Products in use or planned: {n_active}. Fully retired in the last 12 months: {n_retired} (own sheet; a contract may still be running). "
         "Products one unit dropped but others still use stay on the main sheet, with a note.", False),
        ("Generic laptops, phones, tablets and printers are left out.", False),
        (f"Product list from the inventory survey export of {long_date(EXPORT)}; collection closed September 29, 2026.", False),
        ("", False),
        ("Internal only. Shared with the budget planning group set by Kenny Boyd. Do not forward.", True),
    ]
    ws.column_dimensions["A"].width = 120
    for i, (text, bold) in enumerate(lines, 1):
        c = ws.cell(i, 1, text)
        c.font = Font(name=FONT, size=14 if i == 1 else 11, bold=bold, color=GREEN if bold else "000000")
        c.alignment = Alignment(wrap_text=True)


def build():
    active = active_products()
    names = {r[0] for r in active}
    retired = retired_products(names)
    missing = sorted(set(KNOWN) - {r[0] for r in active})
    if missing:
        sys.exit(f"[error] KNOWN entries not in the product list: {', '.join(missing)}")
    wb = Workbook()
    ws = wb.active
    ws.title = "Costs and terms"
    product_sheet(ws, active, "Baylor Athletics Technology Inventory: Costs and Terms",
                  f"Final product list as of {long_date(TODAY)} ({len(active)} products). "
                  "Green columns from the survey; gold columns to fill in. For FY28 budget planning.",
                  notes=stopped_notes(names))
    product_sheet(wb.create_sheet("Retired"), retired,
                  "Retired in the last 12 months",
                  "No unit uses these any more; check whether a contract or renewal is still running.")
    guide(wb.create_sheet("How to fill in"), len(active), len(retired))
    os.makedirs(DELIV, exist_ok=True)
    path = os.path.join(DELIV, STEM + ".xlsx")
    if os.path.exists(path):
        sys.exit(f"[error] {path} exists; it may hold filled-in costs. Move it before rebuilding.")
    wb.save(path)
    print(f"wrote {path}: {len(active)} active, {len(retired)} retired")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    build()

entries.name: TaskCreate
entries.description:
Use this tool to create a structured task list for your current coding session. This helps you track progress, organize complex tasks, and demonstrate thoroughness to the user.
It also helps the user understand the progress of the task and overall progress of their requests.

## When to Use This Tool

Use this tool proactively in these scenarios:

- Complex multi-step tasks - When a task requires 3 or more distinct steps or actions
- Non-trivial and complex tasks - Tasks that require careful planning or multiple operations
- Plan mode - When using plan mode, create a task list to track the work
- User explicitly requests todo list - When the user directly asks you to use the todo list
- User provides multiple tasks - When users provide a list of things to be done (numbered or comma-separated)
- After receiving new instructions - Immediately capture user requirements as tasks
- When you start working on a task - Mark it as in_progress BEFORE beginning work
- After completing a task - Mark it as completed and add any new follow-up tasks discovered during implementation

## When NOT to Use This Tool

Skip using this tool when:
- There is only a single, straightforward task
- The task is trivial and tracking it provides no organizational benefit
- The task can be completed in less than 3 trivial steps
- The task is purely conversational or informational

NOTE that you should not use this tool if there is only one trivial task to do. In this case you are better off just doing the task directly.

## Task Fields

- **subject**: A brief, actionable title in imperative form (e.g., "Fix authentication bug in login flow")
- **description**: What needs to be done
- **activeForm** (optional): Present continuous form shown in the spinner when the task is in_progress (e.g., "Fixing authentication bug"). If omitted, the spinner shows the subject instead.

All tasks are created with status `pending`.

## Tips

- Create tasks with clear, specific subjects that describe the outcome
- After creating tasks, use TaskUpdate to set up dependencies (blocks/blockedBy) if needed
- Check TaskList first to avoid creating duplicate tasks

subject.description: A brief title for the task

activeForm.description: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")

metadata.description: Arbitrary metadata to attach to the task

entries.name: TaskUpdate
entries.description:
Use this tool to update a task in the task list.

## When to Use This Tool

**Mark tasks as resolved:**
- When you have completed the work described in a task
- When a task is no longer needed or has been superseded
- IMPORTANT: Always mark your assigned tasks as resolved when you finish them
- After resolving, call TaskList to find your next task

- ONLY mark a task as completed when you have FULLY accomplished it
- If you encounter errors, blockers, or cannot finish, keep the task as in_progress
- When blocked, create a new task describing what needs to be resolved
- Never mark a task as completed if:
  - Tests are failing
  - Implementation is partial
  - You encountered unresolved errors
  - You couldn't find necessary files or dependencies

**Delete tasks:**
- When a task is no longer relevant or was created in error
- Setting status to `deleted` permanently removes the task

**Update task details:**
- When requirements change or become clearer
- When establishing dependencies between tasks

## Fields You Can Update

- **status**: The task status (see Status Workflow below)
- **subject**: Change the task title (imperative form, e.g., "Run tests")
- **description**: Change the task description
- **activeForm**: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")
- **owner**: Change the task owner (agent name)
- **metadata**: Merge metadata keys into the task (set a key to null to delete it)
- **addBlocks**: Mark tasks that cannot start until this one completes
- **addBlockedBy**: Mark tasks that must complete before this one can start

## Status Workflow

Status progresses: `pending` → `in_progress` → `completed`

Use `deleted` to permanently remove a task.

## Staleness

Make sure to read a task's latest state using `TaskGet` before updating it.

## Examples

Mark task as in progress when starting work:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "in_progress"}
```

Mark task as completed after finishing work:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "completed"}
```

Delete a task:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "deleted"}
```

Claim a task by setting owner:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "owner": "my-name"}
```

Set up task dependencies:
```json
{"taskId": "2", "addBlockedBy": ["1"]}
```

taskId.description: The ID of the task to update

activeForm.description: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")

addBlocks.description: Task IDs that this task blocks

addBlockedBy.description: Task IDs that block this task

metadata.description: Metadata keys to merge into the task. Set a key to null to delete it.

# New project scaffold

Every project Eric works on lives in one folder under DEV, is its own git repo, and has a private remote at `github.com/erash11/<name>`. This skill creates that shape in one pass so every project starts identical on either machine.

## DEV root

- Mac: `~/DEV`
- Windows: `C:\Users\eric_rash\Desktop\DEV`
- Football sub-projects live in `DEV/Football/<name>` and are still their own repos.
- `DEV/_DRIVE` is a link to the Google Drive primary storage drive (documents, data, deliverables). Never create a project inside it and never `git init` it.

If the cwd is already the intended project folder, use it. Otherwise ask for the project name only; everything else is fixed.

## Steps

1. Create `DEV/<name>` (or use the existing folder). Do not nest a repo inside another repo; check `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` from the parent first.
2. `git init -b main` if there is no `.git`.
3. Write these files if they do not exist. Never overwrite an existing one; append the Session routine section to an existing AGENTS.md if it is missing.

`AGENTS.md`:
```
# AGENTS.md

Project: <name>

## What this is
<one paragraph, ask Eric if unknown>

## Session routine
- Start: run `git pull`, then read docs/STATUS.md before doing anything else.
- End: update docs/STATUS.md (done, next, open questions), commit, and `git push`.
- Never leave uncommitted work at the end of a session.

## Conventions
- Durable notes and decisions go in docs/, committed. Not in chat, not in cloud project docs.
- Documents, data exports, and deliverables live on the primary storage drive (Google Drive 00_Primary_Storage_Drive), not in the repo. Files over 95 MB never go in git.
- Writing: plain, direct, no em dashes. Documents use the Baylor design system.
```

`CLAUDE.md`: exactly one line, `@AGENTS.md`.

`docs/STATUS.md`:
```
# STATUS

Read this first. Update it before ending every session.

## Current state
- <today>: project created.

## Next
-

## Open questions
-

## Gotchas
-
```

`.gitignore`: `.env`, `.env.*`, `node_modules/`, `.venv/`, `venv/`, `__pycache__/`, `.DS_Store`, `Thumbs.db`, plus any data folder Eric names.

4. `git add -A && git commit -m "Scaffold project"`.
5. `gh repo create erash11/<name> --private --source=. --push`. If the repo already exists, add it as origin and `git push -u origin main` instead.
6. Confirm in two lines: folder path and repo URL. Remind Eric that the other machine gets it with `gh repo clone erash11/<name>` into its DEV.

## Rules

- Repo name = folder name; replace spaces with underscores.
- Never create a repo for anything holding identifiable health or athlete medical data (DexaProject is the precedent). Ask if unsure.
- Do not add a `docs/context.md` unless there is cloud-project context to transfer.

# Teams plan: Software & Technology Review group

Draft, 2026-10-01. Source: Kenny's 10-01 meeting (KB_TechReview_Followup, 20:43-24:30) and
his follow-up email. Kenny asked Eric to "set up where you feel like we want this
centralized" and then communicate out to the group; Eric chose Teams because it is built
for communication and the files sit on SharePoint underneath. Eric's post is Kenny's cue to
send his own introductory email asking the group to start entering information.

## Goal

One private place where a small group fills in annual cost and use agreement term dates for
the department's 184 products, so Kenny can take a summary to ET before the end of November
and use it in FY28 budget planning. The dollar figures must not reach the wider department.

## Who is in it

| Role | People | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Owners | Kenny Boyd, Eric Rash | Kenny sponsors; Eric runs the workbook and the group |
| Members | CR, CRS, KF | Named in Kenny's email |
| Members, Business Office | Cody, Chris, Erin Boyette, Jovan, Callie | Hold the contract and payment records; Kenny said start with Cody, Chris and Erin |

Nobody else. No guests. Confirm full names for CR, CRS and KF with Kenny before inviting.

## Structure: keep it small

One **private team**, not a channel inside an existing team. A private team keeps the files
private by default; a channel in a department-wide team does not.

- **Name:** Athletics Software & Technology Review
- **Description:** "Annual costs and use agreements for department software. Internal only, for FY28 budget planning."
- **Channels (three):**
  1. **General**: announcements, deadlines, Kenny's updates.
  2. **Costs and Use Agreements**: the workbook, pinned as a tab. Questions about a product go in a reply under that product's name so the history stays findable.
  3. **ET Summary**: the draft report for ET, opened once the costs are mostly in (target early November).

Do not make more channels until a real need appears. ITS approvals (Vault, VALD, Databricks)
stay in Eric's weekly tracker with Kenny, not here: different audience.

## Settings

- Privacy: **Private**. Only owners can add members (Team settings > Member permissions: untick "Allow members to add and remove members").
- Turn off guest access.
- Ask ITS whether Baylor has a sensitivity label (for example "Confidential") for Teams; if so, apply it.
- Files: upload the workbook to the Costs and Use Agreements channel's Files, then **+ Add a tab > Excel** to pin it. Everyone edits the same copy in Excel for the web; no emailed copies.
- After the upload, the Teams copy is the only working copy. Rename the Drive copy with `_archive` so nobody edits two versions.

## Build steps (about 30 minutes)

1. Teams > Join or create a team > Create team > From scratch > Private. Name and description as above. (5 min)
2. Add Kenny as a second owner; add the members above. (5 min)
3. Settings: member permissions, guest access. (3 min)
4. Create the two extra channels. (2 min)
5. Upload `Tech_Inventory_COSTS_INTERNAL_ER_2026-10-01.xlsx` to Costs and Use Agreements; pin it as a tab. Open it once in the browser to check the dropdowns and the Summary sheet work. (10 min)
6. Upload the final inventory documents (EXEC_SUMMARY and BY_UNIT, dated 2026-10-01) to General > Files as reference. (2 min)
7. Post the welcome message below in General. (3 min)
8. Tell Kenny the team is live, so he can send his introductory email.

## Welcome post (draft)

> **Welcome to the Software & Technology Review**
>
> Kenny has asked this group to help put annual costs and use agreement dates against the
> department's software and technology, for FY28 budget planning and a summary for ET
> before the end of November.
>
> The workbook is pinned in **Costs and Use Agreements**. It lists all 184 products from
> this fall's inventory (final as of October 1). For each one, please fill in what you know:
> annual cost, who pays, and when the use agreement ends (for example, Kitman Labs ends
> November 2027). Blanks are fine. "Unknown" is better than a guess. Put your initials and
> the date on any row you change.
>
> The **Summary** sheet totals itself as rows are filled in.
>
> This is internal only. Please do not download, forward or share the figures outside this
> team. Questions go in the Costs and Use Agreements channel or straight to me.
>
> Target: as many rows as possible by **October 31**.

## Timeline

| When | What | Who |
|---|---|---|
| Week of Oct 6 | Team live, welcome post, Kenny's intro email | ER, KB |
| Oct 6 to Oct 31 | Fill costs and terms; Erin's CSV merged in | Business Office, group |
| Weekly | Progress number from the Summary sheet in the check-in with Kenny | ER |
| Nov 3 to Nov 14 | Draft ET summary in the ET Summary channel | ER, KB |
| Before Nov 30 | ET summary delivered | KB |

## Open questions for Kenny

- Full names behind CR, CRS and KF.
- Does Baylor's fiscal year start June 1? The workbook assumes so (FY28 = June 2027 to May 2028); the Business Office can change one cell.
- Should Kenny or Eric own the team long term?
- Is October 31 the right target for the costs?

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build the CSV sent to the Business Office (Erin Boyette first) asking for each
product's annual cost and use agreement term.

Run:
    python scripts/build_cost_request_csv.py [--out DIR]

One row per product, in the same order and with the same names as the costs workbook
(Tech_Inventory_Analysis/scripts/build_cost_workbook.py), so a returned file can be merged
straight in. Survey columns are filled; cost and term columns are blank. Retired products
are included with status "Retired", since a contract can outlive the product's use.

The blank file is safe to commit. A RETURNED file holds real figures: save it under
returns/ (gitignored) or on Drive, never in git.
"""

import argparse
import collections
import csv
import os
import sys

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
DEV = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(HERE, "..", "..", "..", "..", ".."))
if not os.path.isdir(os.path.join(DEV, "Tech_Inventory_Analysis")):
    DEV = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(HERE, "..", ".."))   # run from the main checkout
CLEAN = os.path.join(DEV, "Tech_Inventory_Analysis", "clean")

GENERIC = {"Laptop (generic)", "Phone (generic)", "Tablet (generic)", "Printer (generic)"}
KNOWN_TERM_END = {"Kitman Labs": "2027-11-27"}   # per Kenny Boyd, 2026-10-01
PRETTY = {
    "video-analytics": "Video and analytics", "comms-media": "Communications and media",
    "performance": "Performance", "admin": "Administration", "broadcast": "Broadcast",
    "productivity": "Productivity", "medical": "Medical",
    "office-general": "Office and general", "recruiting": "Recruiting",
    "hardware": "Hardware", "equipment-ops": "Equipment operations",
    "academic": "Academic", "athlete-management": "Athlete management",
    "ai-general": "AI tools", "facility": "Facility", "ticketing": "Ticketing",
    "food-travel": "Food and travel", "athlete-stipend": "Athlete stipend",
    "social-media": "Social media", "uncategorised": "Unidentified (being confirmed)",
}
HEADER = ["Product", "Category", "Units using it", "Status",
          "Annual cost ($)", "Cost basis (per year / per seat / per month / one-time)",
          "Paid by (unit or budget line)", "Use agreement start (YYYY-MM-DD)",
          "Use agreement term end (YYYY-MM-DD)", "Auto-renews (Yes / No / Unknown)",
          "Notice to cancel (days)", "Vendor contact", "Notes"]


def rd(name):
    path = os.path.join(CLEAN, name)
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        sys.exit(f"[error] {path} not found; is Tech_Inventory_Analysis next to this repo?")
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        return list(csv.DictReader(f))


def rows():
    statuses = collections.defaultdict(set)
    for r in rd("tech_inventory_long.csv"):
        statuses[r["canonical"]].add(r["status"])
    active = []
    for m in rd("tech_master.csv"):
        p = m["canonical"]
        if m["category"] == "excluded" or p in GENERIC:
            continue
        units = "; ".join(u.strip() for u in m["units"].split(";") if u.strip())
        status = "Planned" if statuses.get(p) == {"planned"} else "In use"
        active.append([p, PRETTY.get(m["category"], m["category"]), units, status])
    names = {r[0] for r in active}
    stopped = collections.defaultdict(lambda: ["", set()])
    for r in rd("stopped_using.csv"):
        stopped[r["canonical"]][0] = r["category"]
        stopped[r["canonical"]][1].add(r["unit"])
    retired = [[p, PRETTY.get(c, c), "; ".join(sorted(u)), "Retired"]
               for p, (c, u) in stopped.items() if p not in names]
    out = sorted(active, key=lambda r: r[0].lower()) + sorted(retired, key=lambda r: r[0].lower())
    for r in out:
        blank = [""] * (len(HEADER) - len(r))
        if r[0] in KNOWN_TERM_END:
            blank[HEADER.index("Use agreement term end (YYYY-MM-DD)") - len(r)] = KNOWN_TERM_END[r[0]]
            blank[-1] = "Term end per Kenny Boyd, 2026-10-01"
        r.extend(blank)
    return out, len(active), len(retired)


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--out", default=os.path.join(HERE, "..", "templates"))
    a = ap.parse_args()
    data, n_active, n_retired = rows()
    os.makedirs(a.out, exist_ok=True)
    path = os.path.join(a.out, "SoftwareTech_Cost_Request_2026-10-01.csv")
    # utf-8-sig so Excel opens names like "Kitman Labs" and any accents cleanly.
    with open(path, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
        w = csv.writer(f)
        w.writerow(HEADER)
        w.writerows(data)
    print(f"wrote {os.path.abspath(path)}: {n_active} in use or planned, {n_retired} retired")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Eric

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build the starting ITS project tracker for the weekly check-in with Kenny.

Run:
    python scripts/build_its_tracker.py [--out DIR]

Asked for in the 2026-10-01 meeting (KB_TechReview_Followup, 9:45-16:42): "project name,
whatever ID, current status, next step, current blockers, date since last communication,
and any relevant details", because what people want to know is why something is not
approved yet, and the answer often sits with another team. Kenny: "a simple Excel sheet
with drop-down qualifiers for status... informal, just keeping us on the same page."

This seeds the rows from that meeting and Kenny's follow-up email. Once built, the Excel
file (on Drive, later Teams) is the working copy; this script is not rerun over it, and it
refuses to overwrite an existing file. Facts the meeting did not give (IDEA form numbers,
contact dates) are left blank on purpose.
"""

import argparse
import datetime
import os
import sys

from openpyxl import Workbook
from openpyxl.formatting.rule import FormulaRule
from openpyxl.styles import Alignment, Border, Font, PatternFill, Side
from openpyxl.utils import get_column_letter
from openpyxl.worksheet.datavalidation import DataValidation

GREEN, GOLD, CREAM, GREY, RED = "154734", "B8860B", "FFF4DA", "595959", "F4CCCC"
FONT = "Calibri"
TODAY = datetime.date.today()
STALE_DAYS = 14   # last contact older than this turns red

STATUSES = ["Not started", "IDEA form needed", "IDEA form submitted", "In ITS review",
            "In security review", "Waiting on vendor", "Waiting on us", "Approved", "Live",
            "On hold", "Closed"]
WAITING_ON = ["ITS", "ITS security review", "Vendor", "Applied Performance", "Kenny",
              "Another unit", "Nobody"]
TYPES = ["ITS review", "Pilot", "Evaluation", "Process", "Project", "Meeting"]

# (header, width, kind)
COLUMNS = [
    ("Project / request", 30, "text"), ("IDEA form #", 11, "text"),
    ("Unit / sport", 18, "text"), ("Type", 12, "type"), ("Status", 18, "status"),
    ("Waiting on", 18, "waiting"), ("ITS / campus contact", 18, "text"),
    ("Our owner", 10, "text"), ("Blockers", 36, "text"), ("Dependencies", 24, "text"),
    ("Next step", 36, "text"), ("Next step owner", 12, "text"),
    ("Last contact", 12, "date"), ("Days since contact", 10, "formula"),
    ("Details", 44, "text"),
]
C = {name: i for i, (name, _w, _k) in enumerate(COLUMNS, 1)}

# Seed rows from the 10-01 meeting and Kenny's email. Keys are column headers.
SEED = [
    {"Project / request": "Vault (Move Health)", "Unit / sport": "Applied Performance",
     "Type": "ITS review", "Status": "In security review", "Waiting on": "ITS",
     "Our owner": "ER",
     "Blockers": "ITS asked for a new HECVAT covering the whole Vault platform; the 2020 onboarding vetting is not on record.",
     "Next step": "Send ITS a status note, cc Kenny. Ask whether attaching all documents to the IDEA form up front would help.",
     "Next step owner": "ER",
     "Details": "Kenny asked for the status note in the 10-01 meeting."},
    {"Project / request": "Firstbeat", "Type": "ITS review", "Status": "In security review",
     "Waiting on": "ITS security review", "Our owner": "ER",
     "Blockers": "Documentation complete; held at the security review step (possibly one reviewer).",
     "Next step": "Ask ITS for the security review timeline.", "Next step owner": "ER",
     "Details": "Example Eric gave on 10-01 of a request stuck with another team."},
    {"Project / request": "GEO lighting app", "Unit / sport": "Softball",
     "Type": "ITS review", "Status": "IDEA form needed", "Waiting on": "Applied Performance",
     "ITS / campus contact": "Andrew Stripling", "Our owner": "KB",
     "Blockers": "ITS replied that an IDEA form is required, though the system is already in the football, baseball and soccer stadiums.",
     "Next step": "Submit the IDEA form with whatever information is available; note the other stadiums.",
     "Next step owner": "Softball (Candace)",
     "Details": "Candace (Softball SBA) asked; Kenny followed up with her."},
    {"Project / request": "ITS SOP feedback", "Unit / sport": "Department", "Type": "Process",
     "Status": "Waiting on vendor", "Waiting on": "ITS", "ITS / campus contact": "Micah Lamb",
     "Our owner": "KB",
     "Blockers": "Micah acknowledged he owes feedback; no follow-up since (about two weeks as of 10-01).",
     "Next step": "Kenny follows up with Micah Lamb.", "Next step owner": "KB",
     "Details": "Kenny offered to be a joint contact with Eric. Status reads 'Waiting on vendor' only until a better option is added; ITS is the party."},
    {"Project / request": "VALD app", "Unit / sport": "Tennis (M)", "Type": "ITS review",
     "Status": "In ITS review", "Waiting on": "ITS", "Our owner": "ER",
     "Next step": "Follow up with MTN staff with an update on the review status.",
     "Next step owner": "ER", "Details": "From Kenny's 10-01 email. Confirm the current status."},
    {"Project / request": "Databricks pilot", "Unit / sport": "Basketball (M) and (W)",
     "Type": "Pilot", "Status": "Not started", "Waiting on": "Kenny", "Our owner": "KB",
     "Dependencies": "Doug's support (given 9-30); basketball staff planning their review.",
     "Next step": "Kenny invites Eric into the pilot discussions.", "Next step owner": "KB",
     "Details": "Databricks would sit above the other data vendors."},
    {"Project / request": "Bridge Athletic", "Unit / sport": "Athletic Performance",
     "Type": "Evaluation", "Status": "Not started", "Waiting on": "Nobody", "Our owner": "ER",
     "Dependencies": "Part of Vault, so it rides on the Vault review above.",
     "Next step": "Confirm whether it needs its own ITS review or is covered by Vault.",
     "Next step owner": "ER",
     "Details": "Online S&C programming; uses AI to read paper cards into data. Purchased."},
    {"Project / request": "Performance / athlete profile product", "Unit / sport": "Basketball (M) and (W)",
     "Type": "Evaluation", "Status": "Not started", "Our owner": "KB",
     "Next step": "Discussion with WBB and MBB.", "Details": "From Kenny's 10-01 email."},
    {"Project / request": "Fan engagement discussion", "Unit / sport": "Department",
     "Type": "Meeting", "Status": "Not started", "Waiting on": "Kenny", "Our owner": "KB",
     "Next step": "Kenny sets up a meeting with JO, Dave Harper, Justin Hoff, Lacey W; Eric included.",
     "Next step owner": "KB"},
    {"Project / request": "Track and Field request", "Unit / sport": "Track & Field / Cross Country",
     "Type": "ITS review", "Our owner": "ER",
     "Details": "Kenny raised it recently (10-01 meeting). Fill in the product and status."},
    {"Project / request": "VueMotion", "Type": "ITS review", "Our owner": "ER",
     "Details": "Older request Eric mentioned on 10-01. Fill in or close."},
    {"Project / request": "Software & Technology Review", "Unit / sport": "Department",
     "Type": "Project", "Status": "In ITS review", "Waiting on": "Another unit",
     "Our owner": "ER",
     "Next step": "Business Office fills costs and use agreement terms; Erin's CSV first.",
     "Next step owner": "Business Office",
     "Dependencies": "Teams group live; Kenny's intro email.",
     "Details": "Costs workbook in Teams. ET summary before end of November. Status set loosely; change to fit."},
    {"Project / request": "Athletics Research Council fall meeting", "Unit / sport": "Department",
     "Type": "Meeting", "Status": "Not started", "Waiting on": "Kenny", "Our owner": "KB",
     "Next step": "Kenny schedules; invite Dr. Sarah Snitcker, Arts & Sciences, FARs Mencken and Upenieks.",
     "Next step owner": "KB",
     "Dependencies": "Annual summary report as pre-read (to be developed).",
     "Details": "From Kenny's 10-01 email."},
]


def build(out_dir):
    wb = Workbook()
    ws = wb.active
    ws.title = "Tracker"
    last_col = get_column_letter(len(COLUMNS))
    ws["A1"] = "ITS and Technology Project Tracker"
    ws["A1"].font = Font(name=FONT, size=16, bold=True, color=GREEN)
    ws["A2"] = ("Weekly check-in, Eric Rash and Kenny Boyd. Update Status, Last contact and Next step "
                f"before each check-in. Last contact older than {STALE_DAYS} days turns red.")
    ws["A2"].font = Font(name=FONT, size=10, italic=True, color=GREY)
    ws.merge_cells(f"A1:{last_col}1")
    ws.merge_cells(f"A2:{last_col}2")

    hr = 4
    for c, (name, width, _k) in enumerate(COLUMNS, 1):
        cell = ws.cell(hr, c, name)
        cell.font = Font(name=FONT, bold=True, color="FFFFFF")
        cell.fill = PatternFill("solid", fgColor=GREEN)
        cell.alignment = Alignment(wrap_text=True, vertical="center")
        ws.column_dimensions[get_column_letter(c)].width = width
    ws.row_dimensions[hr].height = 30

    lists = {"status": STATUSES, "waiting": WAITING_ON, "type": TYPES}
    dvs = {k: DataValidation(type="list", formula1=f"=Lists!${get_column_letter(i)}$2:${get_column_letter(i)}${len(v) + 1}",
                             allow_blank=True)
           for i, (k, v) in enumerate(lists.items(), 1)}
    for dv in dvs.values():
        ws.add_data_validation(dv)

    n_rows = len(SEED) + 25   # room to add rows without re-applying formats
    first, last = hr + 1, hr + n_rows
    lc, dc = get_column_letter(C["Last contact"]), C["Days since contact"]
    thin = Side(style="thin", color="BFBFBF")
    for i in range(n_rows):
        r = first + i
        seed = SEED[i] if i < len(SEED) else {}
        for name, c in C.items():
            kind = COLUMNS[c - 1][2]
            cell = ws.cell(r, c, seed.get(name))
            cell.font = Font(name=FONT, size=10)
            cell.border = Border(bottom=thin)
            cell.alignment = Alignment(vertical="top", wrap_text=kind == "text")
            if kind in dvs:
                dvs[kind].add(cell)
            elif kind == "date":
                cell.number_format = "yyyy-mm-dd"
            elif kind == "formula":
                cell.value = f'=IF({lc}{r}="","",TODAY()-{lc}{r})'
                cell.number_format = "0"
    ws.conditional_formatting.add(
        f"{lc}{first}:{lc}{last}",
        FormulaRule(formula=[f'AND({lc}{first}<>"",TODAY()-{lc}{first}>{STALE_DAYS})'],
                    fill=PatternFill("solid", fgColor=RED)))
    ws.freeze_panes = ws.cell(first, 2)
    ws.auto_filter.ref = f"A{hr}:{last_col}{last}"

    ls = wb.create_sheet("Lists")
    for i, (k, v) in enumerate(lists.items(), 1):
        h = ls.cell(1, i, {"status": "Status", "waiting": "Waiting on", "type": "Type"}[k])
        h.font = Font(name=FONT, bold=True, color=GREEN)
        for j, val in enumerate(v, 2):
            ls.cell(j, i, val)
        ls.column_dimensions[get_column_letter(i)].width = 22
    ls.cell(len(STATUSES) + 4, 1, "Edit these lists to change the dropdowns.").font = Font(
        name=FONT, italic=True, color=GREY)

    os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True)
    path = os.path.join(out_dir, f"ITS_Project_Tracker_ER_{TODAY.isoformat()}.xlsx")
    if os.path.exists(path):
        sys.exit(f"[error] {path} exists and may hold edits; move it before rebuilding.")
    wb.save(path)
    print(f"wrote {path}: {len(SEED)} seeded rows, {n_rows} formatted rows")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--out", default=os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "..", "deliverables"))
    build(ap.parse_args().out)

# STATUS

Read this first. Update it before ending every session.

## Current state
- 2026-10-01: project created after Kenny's tech review follow-up (meeting note
  `SecondBrain/Inbox/meetings/2026-10-01_KB_TechReview_Followup.md`, plus his email).
- **Costs workbook** (built in `Tech_Inventory_Analysis`, `scripts/build_cost_workbook.py`):

  `05_SYSTEMS/SoftwareTechDocs/TechInventory_2026-08/`. 184 products, gold input columns
  (annual cost, use agreement dates, auto-renew, entered by), Summary sheet that totals itself
  and counts agreements ending by fiscal year (June start assumed). Formulas checked on a
  filled test copy.
- **Teams plan** `docs/TEAMS_PLAN.md`: one private team, three channels, workbook pinned as a
  tab, welcome post drafted, timeline to an ET summary before Nov 30.
- **Erin Boyette request**: email `docs/EMAIL_ERIN_BOYETTE.md`; CSV
  `templates/SoftwareTech_Cost_Request_2026-10-01.csv` (189 rows: 184 + 5 retired, same names
  as the workbook) built by `scripts/build_cost_request_csv.py`; copy on Drive
  `05_SYSTEMS/SoftwareTech_Review/`.
- **ITS project tracker** `ITS_Project_Tracker_ER_2026-10-01.xlsx` on Drive
  `05_SYSTEMS/SoftwareTech_Review/`, built by `scripts/build_its_tracker.py`: 13 seeded rows
  from the meeting and email, status / waiting-on / type dropdowns (edit on the Lists sheet),
  days-since-contact formula, red when over 14 days. IDEA form numbers and contact dates
  left blank on purpose. The Drive file is the working copy; the script will not overwrite it.

## Next
- Eric: build the Teams team per `docs/TEAMS_PLAN.md`, upload the costs workbook, post, tell Kenny.
- Eric: send the Erin email with the CSV (cc Kenny).
- Eric: fill IDEA form numbers and last-contact dates in the tracker; set the weekly check-in.
- When returns arrive: save under `returns/` or Drive (never git), merge into the workbook by product name.
- ET summary: draft Nov 3 to 14.

## Open questions
- Full names behind CR, CRS, KF.
- Baylor fiscal year start (workbook assumes June 1).
- Track and Field request and VueMotion rows: product and status unknown.

## Gotchas
- Cost figures never go in git (`returns/`, `*COSTS_INTERNAL*`, `deliverables/` are ignored).
- The costs workbook builder lives in Tech_Inventory_Analysis (needs its clean/ data);
  `build_cost_request_csv.py` reads that repo's clean/ too, so keep both repos side by side in DEV.

Yes. Right now this one project is spread across six places:

| What | Where it is now |
|---|---|
| Teams plan, Erin email, CSV builder, tracker builder | `DEV\SoftwareTech_Review` (repo) |
| Costs workbook builder, final inventory documents | `DEV\Tech_Inventory_Analysis` (repo) |
| Costs workbook, final inventory documents | Drive `05_SYSTEMS\SoftwareTechDocs\TechInventory_2026-08\` |
| Erin CSV, ITS tracker | Drive `05_SYSTEMS\SoftwareTech_Review\` |
| Meeting note with Kenny | SecondBrain `Inbox\meetings\` |
| Shared working copy (soon) | Teams |

Opening a few folders won't fix this; the fix is **one front door per project**. My recommendation has three parts.

**1. One Drive folder per project, named the same as the repo.** Make `05_SYSTEMS\SoftwareTech_Review\` the only place for this project's files, with a fixed layout:
```
SoftwareTech_Review\
  01_Working\     costs workbook, ITS tracker   (until Teams takes over)
  02_Sent\        what went out: Erin's CSV, emails as sent
  03_Returns\     what came back (internal, real figures)
  04_ET_Summary\  the November report
  99_Reference\   Drive shortcuts to the final inventory documents
```
The costs workbook moves here because it belongs to the review, not the inventory. The inventory documents stay where they are, and the shortcut in `99_Reference` points to them. Nothing gets copied twice.

**2. One file that lists every location.** At the top of the repo's `docs/STATUS.md`, add a short "Where everything lives" table: the Drive folder, the Teams team, the meeting notes, and the related repos (Tech_Inventory_Analysis, SoftwareTech_Mgmt_Framework). Your session routine already opens STATUS first, so after a week away you have one file to read, and it points to everything else. When something new is made, it gets a row in the same session.

**3. A trigger so you actually open it.** Before each weekly check-in with Kenny, run `/meeting-prep SoftwareTech_Review`. That skill reads STATUS and the tagged meetings, and gives you a brief on what changed, what's open, and every deliverable path. The check-in becomes the regular moment you come back to the project, instead of relying on memory.

**The general rule, so the next project starts this way:** repo name = Drive folder name, and STATUS opens with the "Where everything lives" table. I can add both to the `new-project` skill so every new project gets them automatically.

Want me to do it? Concretely, that means:
- Create the Drive subfolders and move this project's three files into them.
- Add the "Where everything lives" table to STATUS.
- Update the `new-project` skill.

It's about 10 minutes, and nothing gets deleted.

# Teams plan: Software & Technology Review group

Draft, 2026-10-01. Source: Kenny's 10-01 meeting (KB_TechReview_Followup, 20:43-24:30) and
his follow-up email. Kenny asked Eric to "set up where you feel like we want this
centralized" and then communicate out to the group; Eric chose Teams because it is built
for communication and the files sit on SharePoint underneath. Eric's post is Kenny's cue to
send his own introductory email asking the group to start entering information.

## Goal

One private place where a small group fills in annual cost and use agreement term dates for
the department's 184 products, so Kenny can take a summary to ET before the end of November
and use it in FY28 budget planning. The dollar figures must not reach the wider department.

## Who is in it

| Role | People | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Owners | Kenny Boyd, Eric Rash | Kenny sponsors; Eric runs the workbook and the group |
| Members | CR, CRS, KF | Named in Kenny's email |
| Members, Business Office | Cody, Chris, Erin Boyette, Jovan, Callie | Hold the contract and payment records; Kenny said start with Cody, Chris and Erin |

Nobody else. No guests. Confirm full names for CR, CRS and KF with Kenny before inviting.

## Structure: keep it small

One **private team**, not a channel inside an existing team. A private team keeps the files
private by default; a channel in a department-wide team does not.

- **Name:** Athletics Software & Technology Review
- **Description:** "Annual costs and use agreements for department software. Internal only, for FY28 budget planning."
- **Channels (three):**
  1. **General**: announcements, deadlines, Kenny's updates.
  2. **Costs and Use Agreements**: the workbook, pinned as a tab. Questions about a product go in a reply under that product's name so the history stays findable.
  3. **ET Summary**: the draft report for ET, opened once the costs are mostly in (target early November).

Do not make more channels until a real need appears. ITS approvals (Vault, VALD, Databricks)
stay in Eric's weekly tracker with Kenny, not here: different audience.

## Settings

- Privacy: **Private**. Only owners can add members (Team settings > Member permissions: untick "Allow members to add and remove members").
- Turn off guest access.
- Ask ITS whether Baylor has a sensitivity label (for example "Confidential") for Teams; if so, apply it.
- Files: upload the workbook to the Costs and Use Agreements channel's Files, then **+ Add a tab > Excel** to pin it. Everyone edits the same copy in Excel for the web; no emailed copies.
- After the upload, the Teams copy is the only working copy. Rename the Drive copy with `_archive` so nobody edits two versions.

## Build steps (about 30 minutes)

1. Teams > Join or create a team > Create team > From scratch > Private. Name and description as above. (5 min)
2. Add Kenny as a second owner; add the members above. (5 min)
3. Settings: member permissions, guest access. (3 min)
4. Create the two extra channels. (2 min)
5. Upload `Tech_Inventory_COSTS_INTERNAL_ER_2026-10-01.xlsx` to Costs and Use Agreements; pin it as a tab. Open it once in the browser to check the dropdowns and the Summary sheet work. (10 min)
6. Upload the final inventory documents (EXEC_SUMMARY and BY_UNIT, dated 2026-10-01) to General > Files as reference. (2 min)
7. Post the welcome message below in General. (3 min)
8. Tell Kenny the team is live, so he can send his introductory email.

## Welcome post (draft)

> **Welcome to the Software & Technology Review**
>
> Kenny has asked this group to help put annual costs and use agreement dates against the
> department's software and technology, for FY28 budget planning and a summary for ET
> before the end of November.
>
> The workbook is pinned in **Costs and Use Agreements**. It lists all 184 products from
> this fall's inventory (final as of October 1). For each one, please fill in what you know:
> annual cost, who pays, and when the use agreement ends (for example, Kitman Labs ends
> November 2027). Blanks are fine. "Unknown" is better than a guess. Put your initials and
> the date on any row you change.
>
> The **Summary** sheet totals itself as rows are filled in.
>
> This is internal only. Please do not download, forward or share the figures outside this
> team. Questions go in the Costs and Use Agreements channel or straight to me.
>
> Target: as many rows as possible by **October 31**.

## Timeline

| When | What | Who |
|---|---|---|
| Week of Oct 6 | Team live, welcome post, Kenny's intro email | ER, KB |
| Oct 6 to Oct 31 | Fill costs and terms; Erin's CSV merged in | Business Office, group |
| Weekly | Progress number from the Summary sheet in the check-in with Kenny | ER |
| Nov 3 to Nov 14 | Draft ET summary in the ET Summary channel | ER, KB |
| Before Nov 30 | ET summary delivered | KB |

## Open questions for Kenny

- Full names behind CR, CRS and KF.
- Does Baylor's fiscal year start June 1? The workbook assumes so (FY28 = June 2027 to May 2028); the Business Office can change one cell.
- Should Kenny or Eric own the team long term?
- Is October 31 the right target for the costs?

Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\eric_rash\.claude\skills\closeout

# Closeout

One command that replaces the manual end-of-day sequence: "any loose ends?" → "commit and push what needs to be" → "is this in memory?" → "write a handoff so Codex can pick this up."

Run all five checks, then give ONE verdict. Do not ask permission between steps — the invocation of this skill IS the authorization for the full sequence. Commit and push is standing-authorized for every DEV repo: each repo's `AGENTS.md` Session routine says "update STATUS, commit, push at end", and unpushed work on one machine is the top cause of conflicts on the other. The only exceptions are repos whose `CLAUDE.md` says their data must stay local (DexaProject is the precedent); commit those locally and list them as open.

This one file serves Claude Code, Codex and Cowork (uploaded to claude.ai). Cowork has no TaskList and no Claude Code memory hooks: do what applies there and say what was skipped.

## Step 1 — Loose-ends sweep

- `git status` across **every** repo in DEV, not only the ones named in this conversation. Another session, another harness, or the other machine may have left work dirty, and a closeout that only checks what it remembers touching will say "clear to sign off" over someone else's uncommitted work. Walk `DEV/`, `DEV/Football/` and `DEV/SpecialRequests/`, and report any repo with uncommitted or unpushed commits. The full walk takes about 90 seconds.
  - Windows: `git -C <repo> status --porcelain` per repo. Do NOT use `Get-ChildItem -Recurse` to look for files; it silently skips paths past the 260-character limit. Inside a repo, `git ls-files` is the reliable way to ask whether a file exists.
  - Repos with dirty state you did not touch: commit and push them like any other, and name them in the report so the user knows another session left them.
- Unfinished todos/tasks from this session (TaskList if available).
- Background jobs or workflows still running.
- Anything the user was promised earlier in the session that wasn't delivered.

## Step 2 — Commit & push

- Every repo touched this session: stage, commit with a descriptive message, `git pull --no-rebase` (the other machine may have pushed), push. If the merge conflicts, follow the conflict steps in `dev-sync/SKILL.md` (they are the one home for them), then push and list the file under "Still open".
- Before staging, make sure any new file over 95 MB and any `.env` is in `.gitignore`.
- Local-only repos (CLAUDE.md says so): commit, do not push, list it.
- Also check the three config repos, `~/.claude` (dotclaude), `~/.claude/skills` (claude-skills) and `~/.claude/global-memory` (claude-global-memory). If any has changes, commit and push it the same way, so the other machine's `/dev-sync` picks it up.
- **Push `global-memory` even on a light session.** `daily-backup` pushes it nightly, which is too late for a same-day handoff: work the Mac in the afternoon, sit down at Windows that evening, and anything written to MEMORY.md or handoffs is still only on the Mac. Pushing it here is what makes memory available to the other machine tonight rather than tomorrow. It is the only repo that carries memory across, so treat an unpushed `global-memory` the same as an unpushed project repo: it blocks "clear to sign off".
- Nothing to commit → say so in one line, move on.

## Step 3 — Memory verification

- Check `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log` — must be empty. If not, surface contents and fix the hook issue if obvious.
- Confirm today's transcript file exists at `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/<today>.md` and was modified within the last few hours. On a Cowork-only day it may be absent; say so, it is not an error.
- Run the dev-docs harvest so repo docs reach memsearch: `bash ~/.claude/scripts/harvest-dev-docs.sh` (Mac) or `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $HOME\.claude\scripts\harvest-dev-docs.ps1` (Windows). It copies every repo's `docs/*.md` into `~/.claude/global-memory/dev-docs/`, which is on the index list. One line of output; do this after Step 4 so today's STATUS is included.
- If this session produced a durable decision or new active thread, update `~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (respect the 2,500-char cap; consolidate before adding) or write a Tier A memory file per the memory-system rules in CLAUDE.md.
- **Tier A does not cross machines — mirror it or lose it.** Project memory lives under a slug built from the project's absolute path, and that path differs on the Mac and the Windows laptop, so a Tier A file written today is not auto-injected tomorrow on the other machine. Global memory and the repo both cross; Tier A does not. So for every Tier A fact written this session, ask: is this durable and project-scoped? If yes, it must also land in the repo — `docs/STATUS.md` for current state, `docs/DECISIONS.md` for a decision and its reasoning, the dated handoff for the detail. Treat Tier A as a fast local cache and the repo as the record. If a fact only ever exists in Tier A, assume the other machine will never see it.

## Step 4 — Cross-harness handoff

This is the **canonical durable handoff** — the one future sessions and other harnesses read. (For a mid-session, chat-only summary before `/clear`, that's the `session-handoff` skill; the mattpocock `handoff` skill writes to the OS temp dir and is not durable — don't rely on it for cross-session state.)

If real work happened this session (not just Q&A), write a handoff to
`<repo>/docs/handoffs/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md` (or `~/.claude/global-memory/handoffs/` if no repo fits):

- What was being worked on and why
- Decisions made (with the reasoning that would be lost)
- Exact file paths of everything created or modified this session
- Next actions, most important first
- Anything mid-flight (open questions, awaited inputs)

Plain markdown, no harness-specific syntax — Codex, Antigravity, or a fresh Claude session must be able to resume from it. Commit it with the Step 2 commit when in a repo.

**Always, in every repo touched (even for light sessions): update `docs/STATUS.md`.** It is the file the next session reads first, on either machine, in any harness. Rewrite the sections in place, keep it short:

- `## Current state` — two to five lines on where things stand today
- `## Next` — most important first
- `## Open questions` — decisions waiting on Eric
- `## Gotchas` — anything that will bite the next session

The dated handoff file is the detailed record; STATUS.md is the summary. Do Step 4 before the Step 2 commit so both land in the same push.

## Step 5 — Verdict

End with a single short report:

```
## Closeout — <date>

**Committed & pushed:** <repos + one-line summary, or "nothing to commit">
**STATUS.md:** updated in <repos>
**Memory:** captured ✓ / issue found: <what> / skipped (Cowork, no hooks)
**Handoff:** <path, or "not needed — no substantive work">
**Still open:** <numbered list, or "none">

Clear to sign off. / Not clear: <the one thing blocking>.
```

"Clear to sign off" means: every touched repo is pushed (or is a declared local-only repo). If anything is unpushed, the verdict is "Not clear" and the unpushed repo is the one thing blocking.

Every file created or modified during the session must appear somewhere in the report with its full path — "where did this save?" should never need to be asked.

## Rules

- Push every touched DEV repo. Do not leave the laptop with unpushed work; the other machine pulls from GitHub, not from this disk.
- Never skip Step 3 — memory capture failing silently is the user's top recurring worry.
- If a check fails and the fix is quick and safe (restage a file, clear a stale lock), fix it and note it. If the fix is risky, list it under "Still open" instead.
- Total output should fit on one screen. The user is leaving; brevity is the deliverable.

lines: +source: "z_6M5r7031A, SSAC19, The True Cost of Tommy John Surgery in Major League Baseball"
+# Many MLB Pitchers Do Not Return to Prior Durability After UCL Reconstruction

+**What it is** — Dr. Eric McNally (sports medicine orthopedic surgeon and Detroit Lions team physician, per the host, z_6M5r7031A [00:00]) reports public-data cohort results on ulnar collateral ligament (UCL) reconstruction, "Tommy John surgery," in Major League Baseball pitchers. The speaker says he was told early on that the surgery "works for everybody" (z_6M5r7031A [09:13]).
+- **Cohort:** 150 MLB pitchers who had the surgery, of whom 140 were "established," defined as pitching in 10 or more games in a season (z_6M5r7031A [09:13]).
+- **Not back:** 20% of the established pitchers never pitched in the majors again (z_6M5r7031A [09:13] to [09:43]).

+- **Back, but reduced:** "one out of three" came back but never reached 10 games a year again, pitching one or two games (z_6M5r7031A [09:43]). The caption does not say whether the denominator is all 140 or only those who returned.
+- **Those who returned:** a statistically significant decline in "numerous pitching metrics" (z_6M5r7031A [09:43] to [10:13]). The metrics and effect sizes are not named or shown.

+- **Value curve:** wins above replacement (WAR) fell over the 3 years before surgery and took 3 years after return to reach the pre-surgery level. With 12 to 18 months to get back to the majors, he puts the full path at about four to four and a half years (z_6M5r7031A [10:13] to [10:43]).

+- **Controls:** in Q&A he says the first data set used age-matched controls and the second was not controlled for starter versus reliever (z_6M5r7031A [18:19]). On recovery by age, the numbers were too small to separate, and the pattern looked like the natural trend with age (z_6M5r7031A [18:50]).

+**Why it works** — The speaker gives no mechanism for the post-surgery decline. He does say professional tears are usually attritional, a slow wearing down with pathology building up in the elbow (z_6M5r7031A [26:13]). Inference: a WAR decline that starts three years before surgery fits that account, but the talk does not link the two.

+**When to apply** — As a reality check on the idea that reconstruction restores a pitcher to prior form, and as an outside comparison when explaining return-to-play expectations for a throwing athlete. Eric's baseline: Applied Performance's stated role in return to performance is to supply information that supports Athletic Performance and Athletic Medicine decisions, not to make the final decision (Explicit, Baylor Applied Performance Playbook p.6). Inference: the figures are context for those conversations, to be handled by Athletic Medicine.

+**When NOT to apply** — This is professional baseball pitching, "one position of one sport" by the speaker's own description (z_6M5r7031A [21:54]). Do not read it across to football, to college athletes, or to Baylor injury types. The period of the 150-pitcher cohort is not stated. The "one out of three" denominator is ambiguous in the captions. The second WAR analysis was uncontrolled (z_6M5r7031A [18:19]). The pitching metrics that declined are not named. This is one surgeon's group reporting public-data analyses, not a controlled comparison with non-operative care. Eric's baseline: the baseline holds no specific return-to-play criteria to compare against (Explicit principle, gap in criteria, Playbook p.6; a written protocol exists in the UE and LE rehab templates, interview Q4a, not yet read by Flint).

+**Example** — The speaker's own definition: an "established" pitcher is one with 10 or more games in a season, so "never returned" means never again at the major league level at all (z_6M5r7031A [09:13] to [09:43]). Inference: 20% of 140 is 28 pitchers; the speaker gives only the percentage.

+**Related** — [[claim--salary-cost-of-ucl-rehab-2004-2014]] (same speaker, same public-data approach). [[framework--expected-value-decision-analysis-for-treatment-choice]] (the model these outcomes would feed). Reciprocal-link suggestion: [[framework--evidence-stacking-before-acting]] in the Old Bull library (a single dramatic result, here surgery, should not settle a decision).
+source: "40NV3_u9tYY, SSAC17, NFL Player Assessment Test: Using Psychological Tests to Predict Player Performance"
+# Validate an Assessment Before Using It: Score Early, Rate Later, Correlate

+**What it is** — The first speaker (caption spelling "Ken yuso"; he thanks co-authors "Charles sheram" and Harold Goldstein, 40NV3_u9tYY [00:03]) describes a three-step validation of the NFL's one-hour psychological test. His background: industrial and organizational psychologists, "heavy litigation, employment discrimination" work, where "you have to demonstrate that what you're measuring actually is connected to some meaningful outcome" (40NV3_u9tYY [08:21], [08:52]). Design as reported:

+- **Predictor:** the assessment taken at the combine before any NFL playing time; 1,500 player scores over three years, about 330 combine participants a year plus a "Super Regional" (40NV3_u9tYY [08:52]).

+- **Criteria:** team coaches' ratings on about 24 dimensions after the player had been on the team at least a year, with about 70% participation across all 32 teams per year (40NV3_u9tYY [09:22], [09:54]); also on-field metrics (penalties per play, yards per penalty) and injuries (40NV3_u9tYY [16:35], [17:37]).

+- **Results (decimal points are garbled in the captions: "0 28", "about3", "a0 29", "about 35"):** about 0.28 overall, about 0.3 for the cognitive composite, about 0.29 for the personality composite, about 0.35 combined (40NV3_u9tYY [10:24], [10:56], [11:26], [15:33]). He calls the correlations "uncorrected", "extremely conservative" and good for behavioral science (40NV3_u9tYY [10:24]).
+He adds that "no test as a crystal ball" and that the test is meant as an addition to physical and skills measures (40NV3_u9tYY [11:57], [10:24]).

+**Why it works** — The speaker's reasoning is the standard predictive validity logic: measure first, then check against what happens later (40NV3_u9tYY [09:54]: "a classic validation study"). The mechanism by which a trait score would produce coach ratings is not given. Inference: the key protection is that the predictor is collected before the outcome exists, which the speaker describes, though the talk does not say whether coaches saw the test results (see the limits below).

+**When to apply** — When deciding whether to add or keep a test. Eric's baseline: Eric (interview 2026-09-28, Q3): "If it doesn't answer a question anyone has, or a direct need, then it doesn't have a place." Eric's baseline (explicit, `2026-02-20-sportsmith-6otb-nordbord-er.md`): "Inconsistent data from a good test is still bad data." Inference: a before-and-after check of a candidate Baylor measure against a later outcome (a coach rating, an availability record) is a cheap way to meet that rule, with the outcome chosen first.

+**When NOT to apply** — Confidence is supported, not proven: the speakers report the method and correlations, but give no confidence intervals, no subgroup sizes and no position splits. The main criterion is coach opinion, not performance. The talk does not say whether coaches saw the test scores before rating (40NV3_u9tYY [09:22], per the summary's limits). The speakers run the assessment, so this is not an independent evaluation, and co-author Harold Goldstein was absent (40NV3_u9tYY [00:03]). Participation was 70% of teams in a year, so non-response is possible, and the sample is rookies and early-career players only. Correlations near 0.3 explain about 9% of variance (Inference: arithmetic on r squared), so use them for broad sorting, not individual calls.

+**Example** — The speakers' own: the test scores taken at the combine against ratings given a year or more later for "learn the game readily", mental errors, decisions under stress, leadership, work ethic and similar dimensions (40NV3_u9tYY [10:56], [11:26]).

+**Related** — [[claim--score-bands-map-to-coach-rating-odds]], [[claim--decisions-under-stress-needs-ability-plus-stress-tolerance]], [[principle--add-standardized-psychological-data-as-increment-not-substitute]]; existing library: [[heuristic--fix-protocol-before-trusting-a-noisy-metric]] (Old Bull), and the research brief [[farrell-2024-beyond-the-box-score-using-psychological-metrics-to-forecast-nba-success]].

lines: +source: "z_6M5r7031A, SSAC19, The True Cost of Tommy John Surgery in Major League Baseball"
+# Faster Pitches Put More Stress on the Elbow, Youth and Professional

+**What it is** — Dr. Eric McNally's group at Henry Ford uses a wearable sleeve that detects stress and torque at the medial elbow, "right where the UCL is" (z_6M5r7031A [04:09]). He reports that, "study after study," the faster the pitch, the more elbow stress, and that this is pitch speed, not arm speed (z_6M5r7031A [04:39]). He says it holds for a 12-year-old youth pitcher and for a professional, and that it has been borne out in "numerous" independent studies from his group (z_6M5r7031A [04:39] to [05:10]). He contrasts it with older advice to avoid curveballs and off-speed pitches and "stick with straight fastballs" (z_6M5r7031A [04:39]).
+- Arm slot: studies of slot and release point exist, and "so far" slot has not shown increased elbow stress; this is the group's next stage (z_6M5r7031A [22:33]).
+- Device limit: the sleeve relies on a throwing motion, so it cannot measure elbow stress in hitters (z_6M5r7031A [21:23]).
+- Trend: average fastball velocity is climbing year over year, which he offers as one of two reasons the injury persists (z_6M5r7031A [04:09]).
+**Why it works** — The speaker gives no mechanism. Inference: a faster release plausibly needs more force through the arm, so more load at the elbow is plausible, but the talk does not say so.

+**When to apply** — As background when a throwing sport (baseball, softball) asks whether to monitor throwing stress or velocity. Eric's baseline: a test or technology that "doesn't answer a question anyone has, or a direct need" has no place (Explicit, interview 2026-09-28, Q3). Inference: ask first what decision a sleeve or velocity number would change, then check validation (the talk does not describe any validation of the sleeve).

+**When NOT to apply** — The talk gives no effect sizes, sample sizes or ranges for these studies. The studies are the speaker's group's own, summarized aloud. The sleeve's validity is not discussed in the talk. It covers pitching only; he says UCL injury is essentially one position of one sport (z_6M5r7031A [21:54]). The slot finding is a preliminary "so far." Do not use it as a velocity limit for any athlete.

+**Example** — The speaker's own contrast: the old coaching rule was to avoid curveballs and change-ups because of elbow stress, while his group finds high-velocity fastballs also impart greater stress, in a 12-year-old and in a professional (z_6M5r7031A [04:39] to [05:10]).

+**Related** — [[claim--fatigue-breaks-the-velocity-elbow-stress-link]] (the same sleeve under fatigue). [[claim--youth-specialization-survey-and-early-surgery]] (the second cause the speaker gives for the injury).
+source: "40NV3_u9tYY, SSAC17, NFL Player Assessment Test: Using Psychological Tests to Predict Player Performance"
+# Top and Bottom Test-Score Quartiles Were Rated Three to Four and a Half Times Apart by Coaches

+**What it is** — To make correlations of about 0.3 usable, the first speaker (caption spelling "Ken yuso") splits scores into high, medium and low; high and low each hold "about 25% of the sample", and the coaches' ratings (a scale of about seven points) fall into matching bands (40NV3_u9tYY [12:27], [12:59]). Reported results:

+- **Intelligence:** low scorers were about three times more likely to be rated "poor performers or disappointments" than stars; high scorers about three times more likely to be rated stars than disappointments (40NV3_u9tYY [13:30]).
+- **High intelligence scorers:** rated low by coaches 13% of the time, good to great 87% of the time (40NV3_u9tYY [14:01]).

+- **Personality:** low scorers about four times as likely to be rated low as high; high scorers rated high about four and a half times as often; 91% of strong personality scorers rated good to great (40NV3_u9tYY [14:32], [15:02]).
+- False positives and false negatives, "the misses", were "pretty low" for the top and bottom groups; the speaker says he is not showing the middle group (40NV3_u9tYY [14:01], [15:02]).
+He notes he was "surprised that the coaches were pretty straightforward" in how they used the scale (40NV3_u9tYY [12:59]).

+**Why it works** — The speaker gives no mechanism beyond presenting the bands as a way to show what a correlation of this size looks like in a cut-score decision (40NV3_u9tYY [12:27], [14:01]). Inference: with about 0.3 correlation, tails separate more clearly than the middle, so band odds look stronger than the correlation alone suggests.

+**When to apply** — When explaining a modest correlation to a coach or director. Eric's baseline: Eric (interview 2026-09-28, Q6): "There is a place for the coach's eye: when something looks off, it can direct you where to look and gather data to investigate further." Inference: reporting "top quarter versus bottom quarter" odds is the kind of statement a coach can use to decide where to look.

+**When NOT to apply** — The speaker states the middle half, where most decisions fall, was not shown. These odds are for a combine test and coach ratings, in the NFL, for players with at least a year of data; they are not injury or performance results. The bands compare the extremes, and 87% "good to great" is of those rated, with 70% team participation (40NV3_u9tYY [09:22]). No intervals or sample sizes for each band are given. Do not apply as a cut score for athletes: the speaker says the test is meant as an incremental data point (40NV3_u9tYY [06:17]).
+**Example** — The speaker's own: a high personality score met a "good to great" rating 91% of the time (40NV3_u9tYY [15:02]).
+source: "Q3i3FOC-dPE, SSAC22, Using Tracking and Charting Data to Better Evaluate NFL Players: A Review"
+# Charted Grades as Labels, Tracking Data as Predictors

+**What it is** — Eric Eager (introduced as being from Pro Football Focus, PFF) argues that football analytics has three data families (play-by-play, hand-charted data, player tracking) that are mostly used one at a time, and that they enhance one another when combined (Q3i3FOC-dPE [01:33], [04:12]). His design, used in three cases: the hand-charted measure is the training target and tracking data supplies the predictors.

+- **Pass rush:** charted pressure (and, in a second model, charted win rate) is the label; predictors are play-level context, the defender's position at the snap, charted position labels, and how fast he leaves the ball in the first second, in the vertical direction and as straight-line distance (Q3i3FOC-dPE [06:16], [06:47], [07:18]).

+- **Linebacker coverage:** the coverage grade is unstable, so he derives a tracking-based trait, play-action "bite distance" (see [[claim--bite-distance-under-expected-is-steadier-than-coverage-grade]]).
+- **Receiver deep speed:** speed over the play predicts the PFF grade on go and corner routes (see [[case-study--speed-adjusted-receiver-grade-landry-kupp-brown]]).

+PFF charters grade every NFL and college game by hand; the NFL's tracking data comes from chips in the shoulder pads and ball (Q3i3FOC-dPE [02:08], [02:40]). The model for pressure is XGBoost, "an ensemble" of decision trees, and returns a per-play pressure probability, not only a yes or no (Q3i3FOC-dPE [06:47], [07:48]).

+**Why it works** — The speaker's reasoning: the charted outcome carries what the hand grader judged and the tracking data adds a continuous, repeatable measure of athletic behavior (Q3i3FOC-dPE [09:19], [10:20]). He gives no further mechanism. Inference: the charted label supplies what counts as success on a play, and tracking supplies how the player moved, so each repairs the other's gap.

+**When to apply** — When one data source labels outcomes but is subjective or coarse, and another measures movement. Eric's baseline: "Data collection has a cost in time, athlete compliance, and staff attention" (Explicit, SportSmith article). Inference: this design reuses data already collected, which fits that cost rule. Eric's baseline: Eric (interview 2026-09-28, Q3): "If it doesn't answer a question anyone has, or a direct need, then it doesn't have a place" (Explicit).

+**When NOT to apply** — The slides are not visible and most R-squared values, sample sizes, seasons and play counts are not in the captions (Q3i3FOC-dPE transcript). The speaker works for PFF and presents PFF tools as results, a commercial view. The tracking data is league-wide shoulder-pad data, which a single college program does not hold (Q3i3FOC-dPE [02:40]). PFF grades come in half-point steps from negative two (caption wording) and graders are not asked to do context math (Q3i3FOC-dPE [26:36], [27:07]). Supported only where the speaker reports a method with a result; see [[claim--expected-pressure-rate-adds-to-pressure-rate-in-predicting-sacks]].
+**Example** — The speaker's pass-rush case: the vertical distance covered in the first second is the most important variable for a pressure (Q3i3FOC-dPE [06:47]).

+**Related** — [[claim--expected-pressure-rate-adds-to-pressure-rate-in-predicting-sacks]], [[heuristic--time-varying-athleticism-instead-of-one-combine-number]], [[framework--receiver-creates-own-context-general-plus-specific-estimates]] — the ESPN talk also pairs tracking data with video charting (teg9SfzpMy0 [28:55], [46:15]).

lines: +source: "pcp9h_M6Ir8, SSAC25, Causal Impact of Offensive Linemen on Pass Plays"
+# CLIP Is Said to Beat Other Methods at Finding Top Linemen and Ranking by Salary
+**What it is** — Jenkins reports three external comparisons (pcp9h_M6Ir8 [06:33], [07:03], [07:34]):
+1. The causal model was "significantly better" at identifying top offensive linemen as indicated by All-Pro and Pro Bowl honors, shown as dark green shading in a chart.
+2. It was "significantly better" in ranking players by salary, "much more consistent".

+3. Aggregated on the 2023 Big Data Bowl sample, there is a "strong positive correlation" with Pro Football Focus rankings, with differences he attributes to PFF having the entire data set while his team had the first eight weeks of the 2020 to 2021 season (caption "2020 2021").
+He adds that the model correlates strongly with completion percentage on individual plays, so teams with better lines complete more passes and win more games over a season (pcp9h_M6Ir8 [07:34]).

+**Why it works** — The speaker gives no mechanism and no numbers: "significantly" has no test statistic, no correlation coefficient and no sample size in the talk. Inference: agreement with honors, salary and PFF shows the metric resembles consensus judgment, which is not evidence that the credit is causal.

+**When to apply** — As an example of what external validation a vendor presents. Ask for the correlation values, the sample, what happens when honors and salary are held out, and whether the model finds linemen the consensus misses (the question that matters for recruiting, Inference).

+Eric's baseline: "Data collection has a cost in time, athlete compliance, and staff attention. When the insight stops justifying that cost, it's time to stop collecting."
